headline: Highest risk is medium: Goose can write/egress and share filesystem state, while the paired Spring samples add no documented isolation or verification path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can read/write the user filesystem, use MCP, and shares state via filesystem across instances; that creates a plausible injection bridge if spring-integration-samples content is placed in the shared workspace and later parsed as instructions. The B profile has no isolation or parsing safeguards documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Goose ingests files from the shared workspace as instructions or tool directives
IF spring-integration-samples content is copied into a directory Goose reads
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Disable automatic instruction parsing from files
Require manual review before Goose acts on file content
Use read-only mounts for sample repositories
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code and files in cwd, has broad network egress, and handles provider keys; if spring-integration-samples is co-located in the same workspace, Goose can expose file contents to external model providers. B shows no data-touching fields, so the leakage path is one-sided but still plausible in default coding workflows.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in Goose's working directory
IF Goose sends file contents to configured model providers during normal operation
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared cwd
Use a separate non-sensitive workspace
Rotate any exposed provider keys
Restrict outbound network destinations
requires-engineering: enforce content redaction before model calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose has filesystem write, git modification, shell, and subprocess capabilities, and its concurrency model says shared state with other instances is via filesystem. B has no write capabilities documented, so direct conflict is not symmetric; however, the shared filesystem plus Goose's mutable operations make collisions plausible if B also writes through external automation not captured here, so uncertainty escalates.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory tree
IF B is wrapped by external automation that writes to shared resources
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories
Serialize write operations
Use git worktrees or branches per agent
Make shared files read-only for one agent
requires-engineering: add locking around mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can produce code and file changes, and B is a sample repository with no documented verification or critical-evaluation behavior. If B consumes Goose outputs as authoritative inputs, errors can cascade into incorrect artifacts or actions. The pair lacks evidence of a verification step, so the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF B consumes Goose-generated files or text without validation
IF Goose outputs are used as inputs to downstream automation
mitigations: Insert a human review step
Validate outputs against schemas or tests
Require provenance labels on Goose outputs
Limit Goose to draft-only changes
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Goose is an on-machine coding/ops agent that handles provider keys and extension tokens, while B is an open-source sample repo with no data residency or regulated-data fields. No specific residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a small compliance gap is plausible from secret handling and logging practices.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Goose's workspace
IF provider keys or tokens are logged or retained by surrounding tooling
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in the workspace
Review logging settings
Store tokens in a secrets manager
Use least-privilege credentials
requires-engineering: document retention and residency controls
